correctness.rationale: All p,q>=2: clique range disintegration with density r^(p-2)(2-r)^q, independent conditional leaf intervals and exchangeability yield the exact covariance spectrum; denominator and normalization checked. pX converges with moments to Exp(1-c) for c<1; sqrt(p)X converges with moments to a half-Gaussian at p=q; strict Laplace maximization gives the c>1 regime. Exact simplex integration independently reproduces full covariance matrices in six small cases and rational moment formula positivity in 323 cases. The asymptotic proof is analytic rather than extrapolated.

originality.rationale: The main new assertion is not the conditional range law alone (obtainable by restricting a bipartite disintegration) but the sharp limit p(lambda_C-lambda_A) with sign reversal at ratio 1/3, the balanced half-Gaussian splitting, and the strictly positive limiting gap beyond ratio 1. Accessible closest primary works determine facet/volume geometry rather than these covariance asymptotics. Related previous geometric computations were checked for whether they already imply the limit statements without further work; they do not state or establish those spectral limits. Residual risk of an unindexed equivalent asymptotic analysis remains.
residual_risks: No claim of bibliographic exhaustiveness; an unindexed or terminology-shifted asymptotic treatment could exist.
The conditional law for split graphs follows from a previously accessible complete-bipartite disintegration; only the new spectral asymptotic conclusion is assessed as original.
At q/p->1/3 the sign depends on finer-scale parameter deviations and is deliberately not asserted.

value.rationale: The quantity is the full canonical covariance eigenspectrum of a natural two-parameter family of Banach dual unit balls. The nonroutine part identifies an asymptotically sharp class-density ratio 1/3 where the ordering of two symmetry-inequivalent eigenmodes switches, and distinguishes a balanced half-Gaussian scaling and a macroscopic-gap phase for ratio greater than one. These reveal structural information absent from facet/volume statements, and the proof gives reusable exact formulas to study related graph-metric deformations.
